verdict.rationale: Elastic Observability documents user-defined alerting rules, including threshold rules on log aggregations and rules at service, environment, or transaction level or via custom KQL. When these rules fire, they can trigger notifications through services or third-party incident management systems. The evidence only shows alert and notification actions on rule firing, with thin detail on the range of automated actions and how they are configured. Missing for 10: documented range of automated actions beyond notifications (e.g., remediation or programmatic callbacks), detailed action/connector configuration docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can create a rule to send an alert when the log aggregation exceeds a threshold.
You can define rules at different levels (service, environment, transaction) or use custom KQL queries.
You can also extend your alerts with notifications via services or third-party incident management systems.
